situation: In the rainy season, Kaltouma sees that the old metal gate of her compound has turned reddish-brown. It flakes and crumbles, and red streaks appear on the ground below it.
A new piece of metal next to it is still shiny. Kaltouma wonders what in the rain and the air can "eat" hard metal, and whether the same thing happens to rocks.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Kaltouma does not know what in the rain and the air damages metal and rocks.
What happened to the old gate?
It became reddish-brown (rusty), and it flakes and crumbles.
How can we protect metal from rust?
We can paint it, keep it dry, and use galvanised (zinc-coated) metal.

qa.q: What is chemical weathering? What is its main agent?
qa.a: Chemical weathering is the decomposition (rotting) of rocks by chemical reactions that change their minerals. Its main agent is water.

qa.q: Study the processes of chemical weathering.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: Chemical weathering is the decomposition of rocks by chemical reactions that change their minerals. Water is its main agent.

qa.q: What is solution? Give an example.
qa.a: Solution is when water dissolves some minerals, like rock salt, just as sugar dissolves in tea. It leaves holes and grooves in the rock.

qa.q: What is carbonation, and which rocks does it attack?
qa.a: Rainwater takes carbon dioxide from the air and becomes a weak acid (carbonic acid). This acid dissolves limestone and forms caves and sinkholes.

qa.q: Why are many soils around Garoua red?
qa.a: Oxygen reacts with the iron in rocks and soils. This is oxidation, which forms red and brown iron oxides (rust).

qa.q: What is hydrolysis? What does it produce?
qa.a: Hydrolysis is the reaction of water with minerals such as feldspar in granite. It changes them into clay, used to make bricks and pots.
Hydration is when some minerals absorb water, swell and become weak. For example, anhydrite becomes gypsum.

qa.q: How can living things cause chemical weathering?
qa.a: Plant roots, mosses, lichens and decaying plants release acids that attack the minerals of rocks.

sum.title: II. Processes and Products of Chemical Weathering
sum.intro: The main processes of chemical weathering are the following:
items: Water dissolves some minerals, such as rock salt. Products: holes and grooves in the rock, and water rich in minerals.
Rainwater and carbon dioxide form a weak acid that dissolves limestone. Products: caves, sinkholes and limestone pavements.
Oxygen reacts with iron minerals and forms iron oxides (rust). Products: red and brown soils and crumbly rock.
Water reacts with minerals such as feldspar in granite. Product: clay (used for bricks and pottery).
Some minerals absorb water, swell and weaken. Example: anhydrite changes into gypsum.
Plants, lichens, mosses and decaying organic matter release acids that rot the rock.

evaluation: What is the main agent of chemical weathering?
Water is the main agent of chemical weathering.
Which process forms clay from granite?
Hydrolysis forms clay from the feldspar in granite.
Why are the soils around Garoua often red?
Because of oxidation: oxygen reacts with iron and forms red iron oxides.
remediation: Rainwater and carbon dioxide form a weak ______.
Minerals that absorb water and swell undergo ______.
Acids from plants cause chemically induced ______ weathering.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. oxidation 2. acid 3. limestone 4. clay 5. hydration 6. biological
end.homework: Ask a farmer in your family where the soil of his farm comes from, and ask if he has seen rocks fall or roads blocked after heavy rain. Write his answers.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Further Study 2: The Impact of Weathering on the Environment.

Correction: the source notes compare oxidation with "old zinc roofs". Zinc protects iron sheets; rust (iron oxide) appears when the zinc coating wears off.
